title: PLATO Candidate Set Profile
description: A candidate set: the matches one run of matching software suggested for a dataset's SpatialEntities, published for people to review and for the dataset's identity relations to point at (promotedFrom). Never inside a place-centric or attestation-centric dataset: a candidate is a claim by no one, and a dataset holds claims. Published once and frozen: no candidate in it is ever changed or deleted, and a later run is a new set. A dataset whose identity relations cite a candidate set should have that set published wherever the dataset is, so that promotedFrom can be followed; a validator that has the set should warn when a promotedFrom names no candidate in it.

@context.description: The JSON-LD context, so that a JSON-LD processor reads the document as RDF in the PLATO ontology: https://w3id.org/plato/schemas/plato.context.jsonld, or a list or object that includes it. A relative address is allowed, as in JSON-LD; null, which would clear the context, is not. Optional: a tool that knows PLATO applies the context whether or not the document names it.

profile.description: Identifies this as a candidate set.

candidateSet.description: About the candidate set itself (plato:CandidateSet, a dcat:Dataset). Its keys are properties of the document node, as a dataset's 'gazetteer' keys are.

description.description: What was matched against what, in words; the run's settings are on each candidate (matchParameters).

creator.description: The people or organisations to cite as the candidate set's authors (dcterms:creator), each with a web address such as an ORCID, a name, or both.

@id.description: A persistent address for the person or organisation: an ORCID, a ROR.

licence.description: The web address of the candidate set's licence (dcterms:license).

issued.description: The date the set was issued (dcterms:issued), from which it is frozen. Each candidate's status is its status on this date.

candidatesFor.description: The dataset (Gazetteer) whose SpatialEntities matches were sought for (plato:candidates_for): its @id.

candidates.description: The candidates, each with its own @id under this set's IRI. A candidate is listed once: two with the same subject, object, algorithmVersion and matchParameters are the same candidate. A candidate already published in an earlier set is left out of this one: it keeps the one IRI it was given there, and the answers to it keep pointing at that.
